title: Lorenzo Tio's musicianship and harmony
summary: He praises Tio's tone on reed instruments, conducting, harmony and ear, and says he knew little of his Mexico background.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Do you know about the T.O.'s, if they used that French system of covering the teeth?

No, I don't know. I think they did. I think they did. I've never questioned the particular amateur that they used. But I have reason to believe that they used the French. I don't know. I'm not saying that as a positive factor. I have reason to believe because the tone they got out of the clarinet was wonderful. In fact, any reading instrument, good to you, put the clarinet down, pick up the bassoon, give a rich tone, put that down, pick up the oboe, or the English horn. You see? He even played some instruments that I've never seen. He told me about them. There's a, there's an oboe d'amour. Oh, yes. There's an oboe d'amour, and there's, oh, several other reed instruments that he played. He played the English horn, and so forth. Oh, he was good at all the reading instruments. And best of that, he was, the Lord, you know, things like the old one, he was all papa. He was an accomplished conductor. Accomplished conductor. And he was good harmonious, common point, everything else. You know, you could take a little melody that long after you got through imitating and really make a, something back there. Yeah, make a development into something real big. Yeah, development into something real big. And that's what I, I can do a little of it, not much, but that's what I would like to do, to perfectionate myself. Yeah, imitation, fuge, loy teo, just like that.
From what I understand, he graduated from Big Honors in Mexico. Did he ever talk to you about Mexico, anything about down there? Well, he was, he was, that's one thing that was peculiar about him.

He was a drag and kind of talking to him, and very sensitive. He'd be afraid after you knew him, very afraid to say something that he'd be too sensitive about. Oh, well, just like that. So sometimes he'd be puzzled to question him.
Yeah, you wouldn't want to question him too, actually.

So I never got very much about that. The only thing I knew he used to speak about, he used to show me his old books of harmony, and tell me this and that and the other and so forth. And he could harmonize in any key you want, any key. And part is a soft way, you know what I'm saying? You could be singing here and you'd change key and everything else, he'd tell you the key you changed to. All he wanted to know, where you began. Yeah. He'd get, he'd get an idea of a keynote of what key you're singing in. He'd give it to him, where you gonna sing? Money. No. He'd get that tone. Now if it's C, alright. If it's C, call it C. Now you can go on and sing or you can go on and play, and you can modulate from any key. Every key modulates, you can tell you where you're going. Minor, major. He was a, he was an expert. Yeah, I bet he was. I regretted the day he died. But unpretentious. You know when he died about? I don't know. Or do you know if they have any of the family? Somebody told me that some of the relatives may be still living. I don't know. I don't know any of his relatives here. Of course, the young Lorenzo was married to one of the boatswain.
